turnaround_reason: MSP-focused software vendor (RMM, backup, endpoint security) whose stock cratered ~36% to the low-$3s after Q2 2026 when it cut full-year revenue guidance on weak UEM/EDR renewals. Thesis is a bottom-fishing setup on a profitable, 80%-gross-margin SaaS business at a distressed multiple.
bullish_points: High-quality unit economics: 80% gross margins, $544M ARR growing 6% cc, adjusted EBITDA ~$40M (29% margin), positive FCF ~$70M — this is a real profitable software business, not a cash burner
Cheap on every lens: 9.1x forward earnings, ~0.92x book, EV/revenue ~2.0x — a rare valuation for durable recurring software
Self-help underway: new CRO, 6% workforce reduction (restructuring charge), management retooling go-to-market to fix renewals
Stock is basing and up ~23% over the last 30 days off the post-earnings low, hinting the forced-selling washout has passed
bearish_points: The guidance cut was demand-driven, not one-off: EDR pricing pressure and customers defecting/renegotiating in the largest renewal cohort — a structural competitive concern, not just timing
$437M total debt against a $742M market cap; leverage limits the margin for error if renewals keep slipping
Growth has decelerated to mid-single digits; the MSP security space is crowded and price-competitive
Only 5 analysts, hold consensus, target mean $4.68 — modest conviction from the sell side
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings: evidence that renewal rates and EDR pricing have stabilized and that the go-to-market reset is landing; a reaffirm/beat off the reset bar would re-rate the multiple.
suggested_trade: Small speculative spot starter $3.80-3.95; size for a name that could re-test the $2.92 low if Q3 renewals disappoint. Options too thin to use.
key_risk: Renewal/EDR churn accelerates in Q3, confirming a structural competitive problem rather than a fixable execution stumble.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows further guidance cuts or net-revenue-retention below ~100%, signaling churn is worsening rather than stabilizing.
